title: Reskin hanoi
statement: A warehouse robot moves a stack of $7$ crates of different sizes from bay $X$ to bay $Z$, using bay $Y$ as a holding area. Each bay holds a single stack. It moves one crate at a time, always the top crate of a stack, and a crate may never rest on a smaller crate. What is the least number of moves?
hints: Where are the other crates when the largest one moves?
Use recursion on the number of crates, moving the smaller stack twice.
solution: Let $m_n$ be the least number of moves for $n$ crates. When the largest crate first leaves bay $X$, the other $n - 1$ must all be stacked on a single other bay, which takes at least $m_{n-1}$ moves. When it last arrives at bay $Z$, the others are again stacked on one bay, and at least $m_{n-1}$ more moves bring them to $Z$. With at least one move of the largest crate, $m_n \ge 2m_{n-1} + 1$, and moving the stack, the largest crate, then the stack achieves this. Since $m_1 = 1$, we get $m_n = 2^n - 1$ and $m_7 = 127$. Why this works. recursion: the moment the largest crate moves gives a recurrence.
